cheng: Quick heads up — saw a regression in stream p50 after last week's continuous-batcher tweak. Symptoms: delayed first chunk and lower partial-decode hit rate.

hannah: Which change specifically? token_budget target? kernel selection?

cheng: token_budget bumped from 64 -> 96 in the experiment; batcher now prefers longer coalescing windows. Also noticing more selection of fused-attn-v2 kernel vs the mp-attn fallback. profiler snip below.

cheng: ```
model: gpt-small-v2 @ A100
before: encode_ms_p50=11, queue_wait_p95=6ms, partial_decode_rate=72%
after:  encode_ms_p50=27, queue_wait_p95=24ms, partial_decode_rate=54%
kernel_select: fused-attn-v2 74%, fallback-mp-attn 26%
notes: kv-warmup hitrate dropped ~8% for short chats
```

eva: Sounds like two competing effects: larger token_budget increased batching (good for throughput) but pushes first-send later which hurts perceived streaming latency and reduces partial-decode opportunities. KV warmup drop could be because more requests are coalesced into fewer kernels and the per-request warmup path gets reordered.

hannah: Can you dump a trace showing partial-decode decision path? I want to see why early-send gate is not firing.

cheng: Pasted condensed trace: `batcher:queued(12)->coalesce_timer(7ms)->token_budget_check(fail)->encoder:serialize(18ms)->emit` — the token_budget_check failed because accumulated tokens > 96 threshold logic.

will: Proposal: introduce a lightweight safeguard "early_send_threshold_ms" that forces emitting the first partial decode if queue_wait > X OR tokens_in_batch < Y after Z ms. Keeps batching for throughput but bounds worst-case first-chunk delay.

hannah: Agree. Also add a kernel-selection hint: prefer kernel with faster first-token latency when a stream is flagged for early_send. We saw fused-attn-v2 improves throughput but has higher single-request encode latency in our microbench.

eva: Config sketch: ```json
{"continuous_batcher": {"token_budget": 96, "early_send_threshold_ms": 8, "min_tokens_for_coalesce": 16, "kernel_hint": "low-latency-first-token"}}
```

cheng: I'll run a targeted canary: 5% traffic with early_send_threshold_ms=8 and kernel_hint enabled. Will collect p50/p95 for first-chunk latency, total tokens cost delta, and partial_decode_rate.

will: Add KV metrics too: cold_warmup_hits, kv_lookup_latency. If warmup hitrate still drops, we need to make cache prefetch synchronous for early-send paths.

infra-bot: build/ci pipeline kicked off for branch `batcher/early-send-guard` — https://ci.internal/3456

sre-bot: FYI alert: streaming p95 increased > 20% yesterday at 22:40 UTC. Rolling monitor on this canary.

hannah: One more thought — partial-decode scheduling: if we emit early, ensure we keep the same KV-cache pinning order so subsequent chunks benefit. Otherwise early-send could unintentionally thrash KV allocation.

cheng: noted. I'll pin KV keys for early-send paths and add a ~50ms KV-heartbeat to avoid eviction during the first-second of a streamed session.

eva: Thanks. Can you post the canary results in this thread once available? Short checklist: metrics (first_chunk_p50/p95), partial_decode_rate, kv_hitrate, tokens_per_response, kernel_mix.

cheng: Will do. Starting canary now, ETA ~2hrs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

will: If it looks promising we'll roll the threshold to 25% and check cost tradeoffs. If not, rollback and try lowering token_budget instead.

cheng: update: canary results (preliminary) — first_chunk_p50 down from 27ms->9ms, partial_decode_rate up 54%->69%, tokens_per_response +1.8%, kv_hitrate restored to baseline. Full logs attached to the ci run.

hannah: Nice! Please keep an eye on p95 and overall CPU utilization; we might be trading a bit more encoder CPU for user-perceived latency.

eva: Great iteration. Let's add this as a small config option in next runtime release notes and document the kernel_hint semantics.

cheng: filed follow-up PR to add config + tests. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/7890

infra-bot: deploy to canary cluster scheduled at 3332110800

sre-bot: monitoring: canary first_chunk_p95 still within SLO. Closing alert. :white_check_mark:
